These principles were reaffirmed in E.O. 13571. In order to work continuously to ensure that the Agency's programs are effective and meet our customers' needs, FMCSA requests approval to renew an ICR titled, "Generic Clearance of Customer Satisfaction Surveys." This ICR allows FMCSA to continue collecting feedback on FMCSA's service delivery. By feedback the Agency means information that provides useful insights on perceptions and opinions but are not statistical surveys that yield quantitative results that can be generalized to the population of study.

items.title: Realty Action: Modified Competitive Sale of 20 Parcels of Public Land in Clark County, Nevada; Modification of Recreation and Public Purposes Act Classification
items.summary: The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) proposes to offer 20 parcels of public land, totaling 200.64 acres in the Las Vegas Valley (Valley), by modified competitive sale at no less than each parcel's fair market value (FMV) pursuant to the Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act of 1998 (SNPLMA), as amended. The sale would be processed in conformance with applicable provisions of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 (FLPMA) and BLM regulations. A 4.88- acre parcel proposed for inclusion in the sale was previously part of Recreation and Public Purposes (R&PP) Act lease N-75746. At the request of the lessee, the City of Las Vegas, the BLM approved the relinquishment of these acres from the lease. Because the parcel is no longer subject to the R&PP lease, the BLM proposes to modify the R&PP classification by removing the classification from the 4.88-acre portion of the parcel. This modification is necessary because lands that retain R&PP classification are not available for disposal under SNPLMA, and removing the classification makes parcel NVNV106381471 eligible for nomination in the 20-Parcel SNPLMA Land Sale.

items.title: Medicare Program; Medicare Part B Monthly Actuarial Rates, Premium Rates, and Annual Deductible Beginning January 1, 2027
items.summary: This notice announces the monthly actuarial rates for aged (age 65 and over) and disabled (under age 65) beneficiaries enrolled in Part B of the Medicare Supplementary Medical Insurance (SMI) program beginning January 1, 2027. In addition, this notice announces the monthly premium for aged and disabled beneficiaries, the deductible for 2027, and the income-related monthly adjustment amounts to be paid by beneficiaries with modified adjusted gross income above certain threshold amounts. The monthly actuarial rates for 2027 are $418.70 for aged enrollees and $452.40 for disabled enrollees. The standard monthly Part B premium rate for all enrollees for 2027 is $209.40, which is equal to 50 percent of the monthly actuarial rate for aged enrollees (or approximately 25 percent of the expected average total cost of Part B coverage for aged enrollees). The 2027 premium is 3.2 percent or $6.50 higher than the 2026 standard premium rate of $202.90. The Part B deductible for 2027 is $292.00 for all Part B beneficiaries. If a beneficiary has to pay an income-related monthly adjustment amount, that individual will have to pay a total monthly premium of about 35, 50, 65, 80, or 85 percent of the total cost of Part B coverage. Beginning in 2023, certain Medicare enrollees who are 36 months post kidney transplant, and therefore no longer eligible for full Medicare coverage, can elect to continue Part B coverage of immunosuppressive drugs by paying a premium. For 2027, the immunosuppressive drug premium is $125.70.

items.title: Privacy Act of 1974; Matching Program
items.summary: This matching program will support the U.S. Department of Education (ED) and the Department of War (DoW) in meeting the requirements set forth in Section 559(b) of the Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, which requires the Secretary of Education and the Secretary of War to enter into a matching program to identify servicemembers and staff eligible for certain public service loan forgiveness programs. Under this matching program, DoW (source agency) will disclose to the ED, Federal Student Aid (FSA), (recipient agency), information on individuals who, at any time beginning on or after October 1, 2007, were members of the Armed Forces serving on active duty for a period of more than 30 consecutive days or civilian employees of DoW, for the purposes of: (1) identifying whether they made one or more student loan payments eligible to be counted for purposes of the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program under subsection 455(m) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (HEA) and Temporary Expanded PSLF (TEPSLF) program; and (2) without requiring further information from them, certifying the total period of such service or employment for purposes of such program and counting the total number of qualifying payments made by them for purposes of such program during such period. ED will evaluate the information that it receives from DoW to create a count of qualifying payments under PSLF made by covered employees on their respective Title IV Loans (as defined herein). In addition, ED will create customized notifications for covered employees based on the status of their respective Title IV Loans and whether they have already submitted a PSLF and TEPSLF Certification and Application (PSLF form).
